value_chain_position: royalty/streaming pure-play, anchor example for the chain; auto-passes Lane A cash/profit gates
cost_curve_verified: Disagree, and the gap is explained: the deterministic proxy puts the trailing-twelve-month margin on earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation at 78.7%, about four points below the company's own reported adjusted margin of 83% in the first quarter of 2026 and 82% for full-year 2025, because the trailing figure still carries the one-off Sandstorm and Horizon transaction charges booked in the fourth quarter of 2025; the company's own figure is the right one going forward, and it is independently corroborated by the preliminary disclosure of 21 July 2026, which put stream-segment cost of sales at $871 per gold-equivalent ounce against a quarterly gold average of $4,506 an ounce, a cash margin near 81% on the stream book with essentially no cost of sales on the royalty book.
gm_trajectory: Reported gross margin fell from 87.2% in the first quarter of 2025 to 67.1% in the first quarter of 2026 while revenue rose 143% to $469 million, but the decline is non-cash: depreciation, depletion and amortisation tripled from $32.9 million to $90.9 million a quarter, and is guided at $95-99 million for the second quarter of 2026, because acquiring Sandstorm's assets reset their book values upward. The cash margin did not move, holding at 83%.
bull_thesis: The bull case is that Royal Gold has just finished buying a materially better business than the one it owned in 2024, the market has marked it down as though the deals were a mistake, and the cash economics say otherwise. Start with what is verified rather than promised. The company's preliminary second-quarter 2026 disclosure of 21 July 2026 puts stream-segment sales at $311.0 million on 69,000 gold-equivalent ounces at a cost of sales of $871 an ounce, with royalty-segment sales estimated at $137-142 million. Against a quarterly gold average of $4,506 an ounce, that is a cash margin near 81% on the stream book and close to 100% on the royalty book, which carries no delivery payment at all. Unlike a miner, Royal Gold's unit cost is written into a contract: it does not inflate with diesel, labour, strip ratio or grade decline. That is the whole point of the model and it is doing exactly what it says. Volume is growing independently of the metal price. Gold-equivalent ounces went from 67,600 in the first quarter of 2025 to 96,300 in the first quarter of 2026, up 42%, and second-quarter ounces rose about 8% year over year. The forward volume book is contracted and named, not hoped for: Kansanshi gold sales of 26,000-31,000 ounces in 2026 rising to 38,000-43,000 ounces in 2028 as First Quantum's S3 expansion ramps, with throughput already running about 25% above design; Khoemacau's expansion approved by MMG's board with first concentrate in the first half of 2028, targeting 4-4.5 million ounces of silver a year of which Royal Gold's share is roughly 60% at a 90% payable factor; Platreef first revenue in the second quarter of 2026 as Ivanhoe completes its second concentrator; and a royalty-rate step-up at Barrick's Cortez complex from 2.6% in 2025 to a blended 3.5-4% in 2026 against operator guidance of 700,000-780,000 ounces. Reserve life keeps being extended with other people's money: Mount Milligan from 2036 to 2045, Pueblo Viejo into the mid-2040s, Kansanshi with twenty-plus years ahead of it, Xavantina out to 2032. Sitting behind all of it is Fourmile, which Barrick describes as multigenerational at 600,000-750,000 ounces a year over a 25-year life, fully covered by royalties Royal Gold bought in 2022 at an effective 1.6% gross rate, and which contributes nothing to today's earnings. The counterparty list is the strongest single fact in the file: Barrick, Newmont, Teck, First Quantum, Vale, Glencore, Ivanhoe, MMG, Zijin, Centerra. These are the operators an owner of paper claims wants, and no single asset accounts for more than about 12% of net asset value after the 2025 deals. Capital discipline, the sector's usual failure point, is being demonstrated rather than asserted. Gross borrowings went from $965.6 million at the end of 2025 to $595.7 million at 31 March 2026 to $400 million drawn at 30 June 2026, with $1.0 billion undrawn. The dividend has risen for 25 consecutive years, to $1.90 a share, and Royal Gold is the only precious-metals company in the S&P High Yield Dividend Aristocrats index. Most tellingly, the first share repurchase in company history was executed low rather than high: 147,205 shares at an average of $203.80 for $30 million during the second quarter of 2026, after the shares had fallen roughly a third from their high, and management explicitly ruled out borrowing to fund it. The logic the chief executive gave in the first-quarter 2026 call is the bull case in one sentence: buying back stock at 1.4 times net asset value beats buying assets the sector is pricing at 1.7 times. Finally, the screener's own valuation stack is broken here in a way that works against the stock. Trailing free cash flow reads negative $244 million and four of five models show a margin of safety of minus 100%, but operating cash flow was positive $862 million; the negative figure is $1.107 billion of portfolio purchases, chiefly the $1 billion Kansanshi stream. For a royalty company, buying a royalty is an acquisition, not maintenance spending. Conditions the bull case needs: gold holding roughly at or above today's $4,154 an ounce; the Khoemacau, Platreef and Kansanshi ramps arriving on the disclosed schedule; the revolver cleared as management targets by the fourth quarter of 2026; and the repurchase authorisation continuing to be used at these prices.
bear_thesis: The bear case is not that Royal Gold is a bad business. It is that investors are being asked to pay a full price for earnings struck at a gold price near an all-time high, by a management team that has just demonstrated its returns can be diluted. Three things have to be taken seriously. First, and most concretely, the metal has turned and the torque cuts both ways. Gold peaked at $5,366 an ounce on 1 March 2026 and trades at $4,153.90 today, roughly 23% lower and about 9% below its own 200-day average of $4,587. Royal Gold realised roughly $4,871 a gold-equivalent ounce in the first quarter of 2026 and the company states a $4,506 average for the second quarter. The third quarter to date is averaging near $4,085. The deterministic torque estimate says a 10% move in the metal swings earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation by about 12.7%, and the measured sensitivity to gold is 1.25 times. Applied symmetrically, the roughly 9% step down from the second-quarter deck already in the tape takes about 11-12% out of the earnings run rate before a single ounce of volume is lost, and it lands in the November print. If gold retraces to $3,400 an ounce, where it traded as recently as August 2025, cash earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation fall from a second-quarter-deck run rate near $1.48 billion to roughly $1.07 billion, a 28% cut, because corporate overhead of about $70 million a year does not shrink and part of the stream cost of sales is fixed in dollars rather than a percentage of spot. Second, the 2025 acquisition programme has not yet earned its cost of capital. Return on invested capital was 8.2% and return on equity 9.0% for 2025 - the lowest in the peer set, against Wheaton Precious Metals at 18.1%, Franco-Nevada at 14.3%, OR Royalties at 13.9% and Triple Flag at 11.6%. The share count went from 65.8 million to 85.0 million, a 29% increase, to buy a development-heavy portfolio at metal prices that were then making history. Management effectively conceded the arithmetic in the first-quarter 2026 call: sector assets were being priced at 1.7 times net asset value while its own paper traded below 1.4 times. Paying 1.7 with currency worth 1.4 transfers value away from existing owners, and the shares are down roughly 32% from their $306.25 high since. Third, reported earnings will look worse than cash earnings for years. Purchase accounting reset the acquired asset values upward, so depletion tripled from $32.9 million a quarter to $90.9 million, guided at $95-99 million for the second quarter of 2026, with a further $12 million of depreciation from the Relief Canyon settlement. Reported gross margin has already fallen from 87.2% to 67.1%. Quantitative screens read the reported line, which is why Zacks moved the shares to its lowest rank twice, on 22 June and 13 July 2026. Then the smaller cuts. The claim that a royalty company never writes cheques is only true of the producing book: Royal Gold funded $70 million into Hod Maden and paid a $50 million Warintza advance in the second quarter of 2026 alone, and SSR Mining's strategic review of its own Hod Maden interest is still unresolved. The Pueblo Viejo silver deferral stood at 1.97 million ounces and requires recovery above 52.5% before any of it is delivered; management told investors more than a year ago to temper expectations, and the ore feed is weathered stockpile material for another five years. Antamina and the other net-profit interests are, in the chief executive's own words, impossible to estimate, with almost no visibility. And no insider has bought a share on the open market against 18 disposals totalling 18,048 shares - the company is buying its stock while the people running it are not. What confirms the bear case: gold failing to reclaim its 200-day average of $4,587 through the autumn; the third-quarter print in November showing the earnings step-down without offsetting volume; the repurchase authorisation going unused after the initial $30 million; or a slip in the Khoemacau or Platreef schedules. In that world the adverse sum-of-the-parts lands near $153 a share, essentially where the stock bottomed at $156.44 in the past twelve months.
sop_bull: Favourable case: about $315 a share. Valued at a gold deck near the 200-day average of $4,587 an ounce, with the ramps arriving and the market re-rating the enlarged portfolio toward the large-cap royalty multiple. Stream segment: cash margin of about $1,020 million a year (revenue of roughly $1,265 million less contractual cost of sales near $245 million at $871 an ounce on about 280,000 gold-equivalent ounces) at 16 times, worth $16.32 billion. Royalty segment: cash margin of about $550 million a year at 19 times - a higher multiple than the stream book because a land-based royalty carries no delivery payment, no counterparty purchase obligation and, in most cases, no term - worth $9.90 billion. Corporate overhead: cash general and administrative expense of about $70 million a year capitalised at 16 times, minus $1.12 billion. Development pipeline not yet paying anything: Fourmile at an effective 1.6% gross royalty on Barrick's 600,000-750,000 ounces a year from around 2032, the Khoemacau silver expansion for 2028, Warintza, the Hod Maden royalty, Cactus, MARA and the Red Chris block cave, risked at $1.90 billion. Non-core investments carried on the 31 March 2026 balance sheet at $411 million, taken at par, $0.41 billion. Net debt: fully cleared, minus $0.20 billion. Total equity value $27.21 billion across 85.0 million diluted shares, or roughly $320, which I round down to $315 to stay inside the arithmetic the parts actually support. For reference the freshest street targets sit at $305-311, set between 30 June and 14 July 2026 with the shares at $194-204.
sop_bear: Adverse case: about $153 a share, assuming the precious-metals cycle turns against it - gold retracing to $3,400 an ounce, the level it traded at in August 2025, with silver and copper following and the whole royalty cohort de-rating alongside. Stream segment: revenue falls to roughly $939 million as realisations drop about 25%, while cost of sales falls only about 12% to $211 million because a large part of the delivery payment is fixed in dollars rather than a percentage of spot, leaving a cash margin of $728 million; at a compressed 11.5 times, worth $8.37 billion. Royalty segment: cash margin of $408 million at 13 times, worth $5.30 billion. Corporate overhead: $70 million a year, which does not shrink with the metal, capitalised at 12 times, minus $0.84 billion. Development pipeline: in a $3,400 gold world the Warintza, MARA, Cactus and Hod Maden investment decisions slip and the book is written toward cost, $0.55 billion. Non-core equity holdings, which are junior-miner paper, halved to $0.21 billion. Net debt: worse rather than better, because the company keeps funding Hod Maden at the second-quarter rate of $70 million and the Warintza advances while cash flow falls, so the revolver is not cleared - minus $0.55 billion. Total equity value $13.04 billion across 85.0 million shares, or $153. The cross-check is that this is arrived at from the parts alone and lands within 2% of the actual 52-week low of $156.44, which is where the shares traded when gold was near $4,000 and the Sandstorm dilution was fresh.
sop_fair_value: $253 a share (base case), with the adverse case at $153 and the favourable case at $315.
sop_breakdown: Base case, marking the portfolio at today's spot gold of $4,153.90 an ounce rather than at a consensus long-term price. Stream segment: cash margin of about $904 million a year, worth $13.11 billion at 14.5 times - a finite-life, counterparty-dependent contract stream. Royalty segment: cash margin of about $487 million a year, worth $8.28 billion at 17 times, the premium reflecting that a land-based net smelter royalty has no delivery payment and generally no term. Corporate overhead of about $70 million a year capitalised at 15 times, minus $1.05 billion. Development interests that generate nothing today - Fourmile, the Khoemacau silver expansion, Warintza, the Hod Maden royalty, Cactus, MARA, Red Chris - carried conservatively at $1.20 billion. Non-core investments of $411 million taken at a 25% haircut, $0.31 billion. Net debt of about $0.35 billion subtracted as a liability, reflecting $400 million drawn on the revolver at 30 June 2026 less cash on hand and allowing for the Hod Maden and Warintza funding still to come. Equity value of $21.50 billion across 85.0 million diluted shares gives $253. That implies about 16.4 times enterprise value to spot-deck cash earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of roughly $1.33 billion, or closer to 15.5 times on the earning parts alone once the non-earning pipeline is stripped out - which sits between the small-cap royalty comparables and the large-cap pair.
risk_reward: At a live price of $207.27, the adverse sum-of-the-parts lands at $153 a share and the base case at $253, with $315 in the favourable case. There is no structural floor beneath the market price: the company carries net debt rather than net cash, there is no deal, tender or fixed consideration, and the $500 million repurchase authorisation is discretionary rather than a commitment. The nearest thing to support is behavioural rather than structural - management bought 147,205 shares at an average of $203.80 during the second quarter of 2026, within about 2% of today's price, and the 52-week low of $156.44 sits within 3% of the adverse case. The distribution is close to symmetric at this price, which is the whole reason for the timing call rather than an entry.
catalyst_status_note: Royal Gold confirmed in its 21 July 2026 preliminary release that final second-quarter 2026 results will be issued after the close on Wednesday 5 August 2026, with the conference call at noon Eastern on Thursday 6 August 2026 - a firm, scheduled, company-confirmed event one day from now, which the input metrics independently corroborate with a two-day countdown to the next earnings date. The honest qualifier is that the same 21 July release already published the load-bearing numbers - stream sales of $311.0 million on 69,000 gold-equivalent ounces at $871 an ounce of cost of sales, royalty sales estimated at $137-142 million, depreciation of $95-99 million, $200 million of debt repaid leaving $400 million drawn, and 147,205 shares repurchased at $203.80 - so the residual information in the print is the final royalty figure, the outlook commentary and whether the repurchase has continued into the third quarter. In this lane the status is descriptive only and carries no weight in the verdict either way; dated-event asymmetry is the other book's job.
peer_comps_note: Measured against the chain map's true competitors on enterprise value to trailing earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation: Wheaton Precious Metals at 21.0 times, Franco-Nevada at 20.6 times, OR Royalties at 15.7 times and Triple Flag at 15.1 times, all four carrying net cash. Sandstorm is no longer a live comparable - Royal Gold acquired it on 20 October 2025 and the quote is frozen at its last trade. Royal Gold's own trailing multiple of about 17.5 times is not comparable to those figures, because its trailing twelve months blends four pre-merger quarters at a 65.8 million share count with one post-merger quarter at 85.0 million and carries the fourth-quarter 2025 transaction charges. On the run rate that matters - first-half 2026 annualised at roughly $1.57 billion, or about $1.33 billion marked to today's spot gold - the multiple is 11.4 to 13.5 times. That is a genuine discount to the large-cap pair and a modest one to the small-cap pair, and some of it is deserved: Royal Gold's return on invested capital of 8.2% is the lowest of the five, it is the only one with net debt, and it carries more copper and base-metal exposure. What it has that the small-cap pair does not is scale, an average of under 12% of net asset value in any single asset, top-tier operators throughout, and 25 consecutive years of dividend increases. A 15 to 17 times multiple on the earning parts is where the evidence puts it, which is what the base case applies.
consensus_delta: The disagreement with the market is about the metal price being underwritten, not about the business. The freshest street targets cluster at $305-311, set between 30 June and 14 July 2026 with the shares at $194-204, against a consensus of $301.50 and a median of $307.50 from thirteen brokers. To arrive there, an analyst has to be marking the portfolio at a long-term gold price near or above the 200-day average of $4,587 an ounce and giving close to full credit to a development pipeline that pays nothing today. Spot is $4,153.90, roughly 9% below that average and 23% below the $5,366 peak set on 1 March 2026. Marking the same parts at the price the market is actually paying today produces $253, some 16-18% below the street. That is the disagreement: not direction, deck. Where I part company with the bears is the opposite error. Zacks moved the shares to its lowest rank on 22 June and again on 13 July 2026, which is an estimate-revision signal reading a reported earnings line that purchase accounting has structurally depressed - depletion tripled from $32.9 million a quarter to $90.9 million and is guided at $95-99 million, with another $12 million of depreciation from the Relief Canyon settlement, none of it cash. Reported gross margin fell from 87.2% to 67.1% while the cash margin never left 83%. A model that reads the reported line will keep marking this business down for reasons that have nothing to do with its economics. There is also a specific, checkable factual error embedded in the screener's own stack, which is worth naming because it will be embedded in other people's models too: trailing free cash flow reads negative $244 million and four of the five valuation models return a margin of safety of minus 100%. Operating cash flow was positive $862 million. The negative number is $1.107 billion of portfolio purchases, chiefly the $1 billion Kansanshi stream. Treating a royalty acquisition as maintenance capital expenditure values a royalty company at approximately nothing, and the associated 11.5-month runway figure is meaningless against $1.0 billion of undrawn revolver capacity.
valley_of_death: The next two quarters carry a quantified, already-visible earnings step-down, and it is arithmetic rather than speculation. Royal Gold realised roughly $4,871 a gold-equivalent ounce in the first quarter of 2026. The company states a $4,506 average for the second quarter. The third quarter to date, taking daily settlements through 4 August 2026, is averaging near $4,085 - about 9% below the second-quarter deck and 16% below the first. On the deterministic torque estimate, where a 10% move in the metal swings earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation by about 12.7%, that is roughly an 11-12% cut to the earnings run rate before any change in volume, landing in the November print. The reported line will look worse still, because depletion is running at $95-99 million a quarter against $32.9 million a year ago. There is a second-order effect that will make the sequence confusing. Royal Gold's stream sales lag mine production by roughly six months on concentrate assets - management put the port, shipping and smelting lag at five to six months in the second-quarter 2025 call. The ounces sold in the third and fourth quarters of 2026 were produced when the metal was higher, so the reported deterioration will be muted this year and then reverse into 2027 if gold stays at these levels. Investors who mark the third-quarter print as resilient may be reading a lag, not a floor. Meanwhile the cash keeps going out. The company funded $70 million into Hod Maden and a $50 million Warintza advance in the second quarter alone, is paying a $1.90 annual dividend costing roughly $160 million a year, and spent $30 million on the repurchase. Against $862 million of trailing operating cash flow none of that is threatening, but it does mean the $400 million revolver balance may not clear as fast as the fourth-quarter 2026 target implies if the metal keeps sliding. Two specific unresolved items could produce bad headlines inside the window: SSR Mining's strategic review of its own Hod Maden interest, which management expected to conclude within months as of the first-quarter 2026 call and which determines Royal Gold's future funding obligation; and the Pueblo Viejo silver deferral, which stood at 1.97 million ounces and requires recovery above 52.5% before any delivery, with weathered stockpile feed expected for another five years. There is no debt maturity wall and no covenant risk - net funded debt is 0.35 times earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, with $1.0 billion undrawn.
positioning_washout: The forced-selling story here has largely already happened, which is a point in the stock's favour rather than against it. Roughly 19 million shares were issued in October 2025 to Sandstorm and Horizon holders - a 29% increase in the count, taking it from 65.8 million to 85.0 million. That handed the register to a shareholder base that had bought a small-cap streamer and woke up owning a $17.6 billion mid-cap with a different risk profile. The shares have fallen about 32% from their $306.25 high while gold fell 23% from its peak, and the gap between those two numbers is the signature of that supply being worked through. Quantitative and momentum money has added to it: Zacks moved the shares to its lowest rank twice in three weeks. What has not happened is a capitulation. Average daily dollar volume of about $71 million against a $17.6 billion market value is thin turnover - roughly 0.4% of the company changing hands a day - which means the de-rating has been a grind rather than a flush, and there is no exhausted-seller signature to point at. There is one structurally unusual feature of this register worth naming. Royal Gold is the only precious-metals company in the S&P High Yield Dividend Aristocrats index, on the back of 25 consecutive annual dividend increases. A slice of the shareholder base therefore owns this for the dividend streak, not for gold. That cuts both ways: it is a stabilising, price-insensitive holder while the streak is intact, and it would become mechanical, index-driven selling if the streak ever broke. On the numbers there is no such risk - roughly $160 million of dividend against $862 million of trailing operating cash flow - and management has treated the streak as close to sacred. But it is the one identifiable trigger that would force a block of holders out for reasons unrelated to value.
forcing_function: The immediate dated event is the final second-quarter 2026 release after the close on Wednesday 5 August 2026 with the call at noon Eastern on Thursday 6 August, both confirmed by the company on 21 July. Its content is largely pre-announced, so the genuine forcing function is a sequence rather than a single date, running through the next four to six quarters. First and most decisive: whether the repurchase continues. Management bought 147,205 shares at an average of $203.80 during the second quarter - within about 2% of today's price - having refused a buyback for years, and the chief executive's stated logic was that buying his own assets below 1.4 times net asset value beats buying sector assets at 1.7 times. If the third-quarter disclosure shows the repurchase continuing at these levels, that is the single clearest statement available of where management's own net-asset-value work puts the shares, and it converts an authorisation into a bid. If it shows nothing, the May announcement was a gesture. Second: full repayment of the $400 million revolver balance, which management targets for the fourth quarter of 2026. That removes the last structural difference between Royal Gold and the net-cash comparables it is being valued against, and it is the condition under which the multiple gap to Wheaton and Franco-Nevada becomes hard to defend. Third: four consecutive clean quarters of the enlarged portfolio with no transaction charges - the record management said in the fourth-quarter 2025 call it needed to build, running through the first quarter of 2027. Fourth, and furthest out but largest: the Khoemacau expansion delivering first concentrate in the first half of 2028 at 4-4.5 million ounces of silver a year, and any further definition of Fourmile, where Barrick's own study points to 600,000-750,000 ounces a year over 25 years against Royal Gold's 1.6% gross royalty, with underground development targeted for 2029. What is deliberately not on this list is the gold price. It is the dominant variable in the outcome, but it is not a corporate event and it is not something to underwrite.
moderator_conclusion: This is a good business at a fair price, which is not the same thing as an opportunity, and the honest call is to wait rather than to buy. Take the quality first, because it is real and it is verified rather than asserted. Royal Gold's unit cost is $871 per gold-equivalent ounce, written into contracts and disclosed by the company on 21 July 2026, against a gold price of $4,506 an ounce in the quarter just ended - a cash margin near 81% on the stream book and effectively 100% on the royalty book. That cost does not inflate with diesel, labour or grade, which is precisely the property a miner cannot buy. The proxy metrics understate this at 78.7%, four points below the company's reported 83%, purely because the trailing window still contains the Sandstorm and Horizon transaction charges. Behind those margins sit roughly 80 producing and 30 development interests operated by Barrick, Newmont, Teck, First Quantum, Vale, Glencore, Ivanhoe, MMG, Zijin and Centerra, with no single asset above about 12% of net asset value and reserve lives being extended on other companies' balance sheets - Mount Milligan to 2045, Pueblo Viejo into the mid-2040s, Kansanshi twenty-plus years. The forensic record is clean in the ways this sector usually is not: guidance delivered inside every 2025 range through two operator disappointments, ounces deliberately excluded from headline counts when including them would have flattered, no promotional language at the moments a promoter would reach for it, 25 consecutive years of dividend increases, debt cut from $965.6 million to $400 million drawn in six months, and a first-ever share repurchase executed at $203.80 after a one-third decline rather than at the top. On capital discipline the verdict is mixed but with the ledger tilting favourably: the sin was paying full price for the 2025 acquisitions - return on invested capital of 8.2% is the lowest in a peer group where Wheaton earns 18.1%, and management itself conceded it was buying at 1.7 times net asset value with paper worth 1.4 - but the penance has been genuine, converting the Bear Creek and Hod Maden equity exposures into royalties, retiring debt ahead of schedule, and ruling out borrowing to fund buybacks. So why not enter now. Because the price already reflects most of it. At $207.27 against a base-case sum-of-the-parts of $253 marked at today's spot gold, the discount is real but ordinary, while the adverse case sits at $153. That distribution is close to symmetric, and the symmetry is not an artefact - it is the 1.25 times sensitivity to a metal that peaked at $5,366 on 1 March 2026, trades at $4,153.90 today, and sits about 9% below its own 200-day average. The torque is stated in the file and it runs both ways: a 10% move in gold swings earnings by about 12.7%, so the roughly 9% step-down already in the third-quarter tape takes 11-12% out of the run rate before any volume change, arriving in the November print. And there is no structural floor beneath the stock - net debt rather than net cash, no deal terms, no tender; the repurchase authorisation is discretionary and the 52-week low is a chart level, not support. Note also that the underlying cheapness rests on earnings struck at a gold price that is extraordinary by any long-run standard. Eleven to thirteen times forward enterprise value to earnings is a genuine discount to Wheaton at 21 times and Franco-Nevada at 20.6, but it is eleven to thirteen times peak-metal earnings, and that is the reason the value case, judged on valuation and forensics alone, earns a four rather than a five. What I am waiting for is specific, and it is a price or a confirmation, not a mood. Either the shares reach the high $170s to $180 - where the base case is a meaningfully larger step up than what remains to the adverse case, and where the entry stops depending on the metal - or gold reclaims its 200-day average of $4,587, which restores the second-quarter deck and lifts the base case into the mid-$260s, or the company keeps buying its own stock at these levels, which the next filing will show. Any one of those converts this from a fair price into an asymmetric one. Absent them, the correct action on a business this good at a price this ordinary is to keep it on the list and be ready.
